title: What If Ice Sank Instead of Floating?

scenes.text: What if ice sank instead of floating? Every lake would freeze solid from the bottom up.
Water is strange. It is densest at four degrees Celsius, not at freezing.
Normally, surface water cools, turns to ice, and floats on top like a lid.
That lid insulates the lake below, which stays liquid at about four degrees all winter.
If ice sank, it would pile up on the bottom until ponds froze solid, fish and all.
Lakes would turn into blocks of ice. One odd quirk of water is why winter lakes still hold life.
